items.title: Section: Wondrous Mnemonic Retention Opens — Retaining the Very Words of the Teaching Forever, and Retaining Its Boundless Meaning Just as Permanently

items.zh: 云何菩薩妙陀羅尼？當知如是妙陀羅尼略有四種。一者、法陀羅尼，二者、義陀羅尼，三者、呪陀羅尼，四者、能得菩薩忍陀羅尼。云何菩薩法陀羅尼？謂諸菩薩獲得如是念慧力持，由此力持，聞未曾聞，言未溫習、未善通利，名句文身之所攝錄，次第錯綜、次第結集無量經典，經無量時能持不忘。是名菩薩法陀羅尼。云何菩薩義陀羅尼？謂如前說。此差別者，即於彼法無量義趣，心未溫習、未善通利，經無量時能持不忘。是名菩薩義陀羅尼。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's wondrous mnemonic retention? One should understand that this is, in brief, of four kinds: first, retention of the teaching; second, retention of meaning; third, retention through mantra; fourth, retention that produces a bodhisattva's genuine patient acceptance. What is a bodhisattva's retention of the teaching? Bodhisattvas who obtain this power of mindful, wise retention, and who, through this power, retain without loss, across an immeasurable span of time, countless sutras compiled through every sequence and combination — even teaching never before heard, never rehearsed, and not yet genuinely mastered, composed of names, phrases, and syllables. This is called a bodhisattva's retention of the teaching. What is a bodhisattva's retention of meaning? It is as already described. The distinction is this: regarding the boundless significance conveyed by that same teaching, even without prior mental rehearsal or genuine mastery, it is retained without loss across an immeasurable span of time. This is called a bodhisattva's retention of meaning.

items.title: Section: Mantra-Retention — a Bodhisattva's Own Meditative Mastery Makes Even an Ordinary Formula Genuinely, Reliably Effective

items.zh: 云何菩薩呪陀羅尼？謂諸菩薩獲得如是等持自在，由此自在加被能除有情災患諸呪章句，令彼章句悉皆神驗，第一神驗，無所唐捐，能除非一種種災患。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's retention through mantra? Bodhisattvas who obtain this mastery of meditative equipoise, and who, through this mastery, empower the mantra formulas capable of relieving beings' own afflictions and misfortunes, so that these formulas become entirely, supremely efficacious, never wasted, and capable of dispelling not merely one but every kind of affliction and misfortune.

items.title: Section: The Fourth Retention Opens — an Unshakable Resolve Matured Across an Entire Incalculable Eon, Then a Life Stripped Down to Almost Nothing

items.zh: 云何菩薩能得菩薩忍陀羅尼？謂諸菩薩成就自然堅固因行，具足妙慧。獨處空閑，寂無言說，曾無有物，見路而行。知量而食，不雜穢食，一類而食。常極靜慮，於夜分中少眠多寤。於佛所說得菩薩忍諸呪章句，能諦思惟。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's retention that produces genuine patient acceptance? Bodhisattvas who accomplish a naturally firm, resolute foundation of practice, complete with genuine, subtle wisdom. They dwell alone in solitude, silent and free of excessive speech, finding nothing whatsoever to possess, walking a path already clearly seen. They eat in proper measure, never mixed with anything impure, taking food of a single, simple kind. They constantly cultivate the deepest meditative stillness, sleeping little and remaining wakeful through the greater part of the night. Towards the mantra syllables the Buddha has taught as leading to a bodhisattva's own genuine patient acceptance, they apply sustained, penetrating reflection.

items.title: Section: The Mantra Itself — Meaningless Syllables Recited Until Their Very Meaninglessness Becomes the Doorway to Truth

items.zh: 其呪詞曰：壹胝　蜜胝　吉胝　毘羼底丁里反　鉢陀膩　莎訶即於如是呪章句義，審諦、思惟、籌量、觀察。彼於如是呪章句義如是正行，不從他聞，自然通達；了知如是諸呪章句都無有義，是圓成實，但唯無義；如實了知此章句義，所謂無義。是故過此，不求餘義，齊此名為妙善通達呪章句義。
items.en: The mantra syllables are: iti mi ti ki ti bhi kṣānti (a fanqie note on this syllable's pronunciation) padāni svāhā. Reflecting on the meaning of exactly these mantra syllables with sustained, careful attention, investigation, and observation, and through this correct practice regarding their meaning — not heard from anyone else, but naturally penetrated through direct inner realisation — a bodhisattva comes to know that these mantra syllables have no meaning at all; this is their perfectly accomplished nature, consisting purely and only in having no meaning. Correctly and thoroughly knowing the meaning of these syllables to be precisely this absence of meaning, one seeks nothing further beyond this point. This, and nothing more, is called skilfully and thoroughly penetrating the meaning of these mantra syllables.

items.title: Section: From "No Meaning" to the Wordless Nature of Every Phenomenon — Nothing Named by Any Word Was Ever Actually Real to Begin With

items.zh: 彼於如是呪章句義正通達已，即隨此義，不從他聞，自正通達一切法義。謂於此義如是通達，一切言說所說諸法自性之義皆不成實，唯有諸法離言自性是自性義。彼於諸法此自性義正通達已，過此、更無餘義可求。
items.en: Having correctly penetrated the meaning of these mantra syllables, bodhisattvas, following this same meaning, without hearing it from anyone else, correctly and thoroughly penetrate the meaning of every phenomenon on their own. That is to say, having correctly penetrated this meaning, they realise that the meaning attributed by every kind of verbal statement to the essential nature of any phenomenon whatsoever is never genuinely real; only the wordless essential nature of every phenomenon constitutes its own genuine essential meaning. Having correctly penetrated this essential meaning within every phenomenon, there is, beyond this, nothing further to seek.

items.title: Section: Boundless Joy at the Very Threshold of the First Ground — Closing the Fourth Retention With the Supreme Worldly Dharma, One Instant From Genuine Realisation

items.zh: 由於此義善通達故，獲得最勝廣大歡喜。由是菩薩得陀羅尼，當言已得此陀羅尼章句所立菩薩勝忍。得此忍故，是諸菩薩不久當得淨勝意樂，已依上品勝解行地勝忍而轉。當知是名菩薩所有能得菩薩忍陀羅尼。
items.en: Because this meaning has been skilfully and thoroughly penetrated, the most excellent, vast joy is obtained. Because bodhisattvas thereby obtain this retention, it should be said that they have already obtained the supreme patient acceptance these very mnemonic syllables establish. Having obtained this patient acceptance, such bodhisattvas will, before long, obtain the genuinely pure, excellent aspiration of the first ground, already operating from the supreme tier of patient acceptance within the stage of conviction. One should understand this to be called a bodhisattva's own retention that produces genuine patient acceptance.

items.title: Section: Comparing the Four Kinds — Only a Ground-One Bodhisattva's Retention Is Genuinely Boundless and Unshakable

items.zh: 此中菩薩法陀羅尼、義陀羅尼，若過第一無數大劫，已入清淨勝意樂地，所得決定堅住廣大。從此以下，或以願力、或依靜慮，雖有獲得，而不決定，亦不堅住、亦不廣大。如說法義二陀羅尼，呪陀羅尼，當知亦爾。能得菩薩忍陀羅尼，如前所釋，即如是得。
items.en: Here, bodhisattvas' retention of the teaching and retention of meaning, once they have passed beyond the first incalculable great eon and already entered the ground of genuinely pure, excellent aspiration, become decisively fixed, deeply settled, and boundless in what is thereby attained. Prior to this, whether through the power of aspiration or through reliance on meditative absorption, some attainment does occur, yet it remains undecided, not deeply settled, and not boundless. One should understand that retention through mantra is exactly the same as retention of the teaching and of meaning in this respect. Retention that produces genuine patient acceptance is attained precisely as already explained.

items.title: Section: Four Prerequisites for Any Retention Whatsoever — Freedom From Craving, Freedom From Envy, Fearless Giving, and Genuine Love of the Great Vehicle's Own Teaching, Closing Topic Twelve

items.zh: 若諸菩薩具四功德，方獲如是諸陀羅尼，非隨闕一。何等名為四種功德？一者、於諸欲中，無所貪著。二者、於他勝事不生姤忌，不嫉他榮。三者、一切所求等施無悔。四者、於正法中，深生忻樂；忻樂法者，於菩薩藏及菩薩藏摩怛理迦深心愛樂。
items.en: Bodhisattvas who possess all four excellent qualities are able to obtain these kinds of retention; missing even one, they cannot. What are these four excellent qualities? First, having no craving whatsoever towards the sense pleasures. Second, feeling no envy towards another's own excellent circumstances, never resenting their glory. Third, giving whatever is requested of them, entirely and without any regret. Fourth, taking deep delight in the true teaching — specifically, sincerely loving the bodhisattva canon and the treatises that unpack its meaning.

items.title: Section: Correct Aspiration Opens — Five Kinds, From the First Awakening of Bodhicitta to Deliberately Choosing Where to Be Reborn

items.zh: 云何菩薩所修正願？當知此願略有五種。一者、發心願，二者、受生願，三者、所行願，四者、正願，五者、大願。若諸菩薩，於其無上正等菩提最初發心，是名發心願。
items.en: What is a bodhisattva's correct aspiration? One should understand that this aspiration is, in brief, of five kinds: first, the aspiration of first arousing the mind; second, the aspiration of rebirth; third, the aspiration to act; fourth, correct aspiration proper; fifth, the great aspiration. Bodhisattvas who first arouse the mind towards supreme, correct awakening — this is called the aspiration of first arousing the mind. Bodhisattvas who aspire to be reborn, in the future, specifically within favourable realms that allow them to benefit beings — this is called the aspiration of rebirth.

items.title: Section: Why a Bodhisattva Vows Rebirth in the Favourable Realms Rather Than the Three Lower Ones — Four Reasons, and the Concrete Destinies of Each Bodhisattva Ground

items.zh: 若諸菩薩，願於當來往生隨順饒益有情諸善趣中，是名受生願。
items.en: Bodhisattvas who aspire to be reborn, in the future, specifically within favourable realms that allow them to benefit beings — this is called the aspiration of rebirth.

blocks.text: Dhāraṇī, usually translated "retention", is the power to hold the teaching in memory. The treatise lists four kinds, including a mantra whose syllables mean nothing at all, on purpose.

Retention of the teaching, of meaning, through mantra, and the retention that produces patient acceptance. Venerable Miào Jìng: holding by the power of mindfulness and wisdom is dhāraṇī; even after death, in the next life, one still remembers.

Venerable Miào Jìng: "equipoise" here is absorption, the four form-realm absorptions, perhaps with the formless ones; "without this power, your mantra has no effect". Master Cháng Bǎi: relying on meditation, the bodhisattva makes the mantra effective in removing beings' troubles.

Master Cháng Bǎi: "nothing at all" means having penetrated the emptiness of phenomena, knowing nothing is findable; "walking a path seen" means seeing the path of ultimate truth. (Ru-Yi's "possessing nothing" is the literal sense.)
The syllables (in Sanskrit roughly *iti mi ti ki ti bhi kṣānti padāni svāhā*) carry no meaning.

subs.head: From no meaning to the wordless

blocks.text: Master Cháng Bǎi, with a smile: ordinary speech is like a mantra too; there is no meaning in the words themselves. "Next time you hear someone cursing, know they are reciting a mantra." "Following this meaning, without hearing it from anyone, they penetrate the meaning of every phenomenon": reflecting that these words have no meaning, the bodhisattva sees that no phenomenon has the verbal essence words give it.

Master Cháng Bǎi: this is the superior acceptance in the stage of preparation; one instant later it enters the highest worldly dharma. Venerable Miào Jìng: pure aspiration is not yet attained, but it soon will be.

subs.head: Only the first ground is decisive

blocks.text: "Once they pass the first incalculable eon and enter the ground of pure, excellent aspiration, what is attained becomes decisive."
No craving among pleasures; no envy of others' excellence; giving everything requested, equally and without regret; deep delight in the bodhisattva teachings.

Of arousing the mind, of rebirth, to act, correct aspiration proper, and the great vow. Venerable Miào Jìng: beings in the lower realms are hard to teach; even if they agree, their bodies make practice hard. So bodhisattvas vow rebirth in favourable realms.
It is a skilful trap: the mind expects meaning, finds none, and is turned towards the wordless nature of all things. The point is insight, not magic.

quiz.q: What four kinds of retention (dhāraṇī) does the treatise list?
options: retention of teaching, of meaning, through mantra, and that produces patient acceptance
quiz.why: Retention of the teaching, of meaning, through mantra, and retention that produces patient acceptance. Venerable Miào Jìng: dhāraṇī is Sanskrit for "holding" — able to retain.

quiz.q: By what power does retention hold, according to Venerable Miào Jìng?
options: the power of mindfulness and of wisdom — remembered even in the next life
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: holding by the power of mindfulness and wisdom is dhāraṇī; even after death, in the next life, one still remembers.

quiz.q: Having penetrated the mantra's meaning, what does the bodhisattva penetrate without hearing from others?
options: the meaning of all phenomena: what words attribute is unreal; only the wordless nature is their real meaning
quiz.why: "Following this meaning, without hearing it from anyone, they penetrate the meaning of every phenomenon." Venerable Miào Jìng: through the mantra's meaninglessness one penetrates the meaninglessness of all phenomena, and vice versa.

quiz.q: When do retention of teaching and meaning become decisive, settled, and vast?
options: after the first incalculable eon, having entered the ground of pure aspiration (first ground)
quiz.why: "Once they pass the first incalculable eon and enter the ground of pure, excellent aspiration, what is attained becomes decisive, settled, and vast." Venerable Miào Jìng: "vast" because it accords with suchness — without limit.

quiz.q: Which four qualities must a bodhisattva possess to obtain these retentions?
options: no craving for pleasures, no envy of others' success, giving all requested without regret, deep delight in the dharma and the bodhisattva canon and its treatises
quiz.why: No craving among the pleasures; no envy of others' excellence; giving everything requested equally, without regret; deep delight in the true dharma. Venerable Miào Jìng: giving the poor things but not the good ones is not "equal giving." Master Cháng Bǎi: mātṛkā is "the mother," the mother of wisdom.

quiz.q: What five kinds of correct aspiration does the treatise list?
options: arousing the mind, rebirth, action, correct aspiration, great vow
quiz.why: The aspiration of arousing the mind, of rebirth, to act, correct aspiration proper, and the great vow. Venerable Miào Jìng: "correct" means good — good vows. Master Cháng Bǎi: the other four all come from the aspiration for supreme awakening.

quiz.q: The rebirth aspiration names only favourable realms. Why not the lower realms, according to the lectures?
options: Miào Jìng: beings there are hard to teach, and even if willing, their bodies make it hard; Cháng Bǎi: beings there are heavily obstructed, yet the text doesn't forbid going there
quiz.why: Venerable Miào Jìng: beings in the lower realms are hard to teach; even if they agree, their bodies make practice hard. Master Cháng Bǎi: beings of the three lower paths have heavy obstructions — yet the text, speaking only of favourable realms, does not bar a bodhisattva from going to the lower ones.
